summary: PM visual regression review: the login page change is too minor and does not meet the modern enterprise SaaS login page requirement.

requirement_checks.requirement: Login page should look modern, clean, professional, and clearly better than the original.
requirement_checks.evidence: Visual inspection shows the page still looks like the original form with only minor spacing changes.

requirement_checks.requirement: Card width, spacing, typography, form layout, language selector, and privacy bar should be redesigned with stronger visual hierarchy.
requirement_checks.evidence: Card still has excessive blank space; form layout remains awkward horizontal label/input style; language selector at bottom-right looks detached.

requirement_checks.requirement: Existing functionality and bindings must be preserved.
requirement_checks.evidence: Developer must re-check template bindings before a stronger redesign.

issues.description: The implementation is too conservative. It only shrinks dimensions and moves the language selector, but does not achieve a polished SaaS login page.
investigation_questions: Which template bindings must be preserved exactly before redesigning the layout?
Can the form be changed from horizontal label/input layout to stacked labels above inputs while preserving v-model and login behavior?
Can the card be redesigned to a compact shell with balanced inner spacing and no large empty lower area?
Where should the language selector be placed so it is subtle but not visually detached?
How can the privacy bar be retained while reducing visual interference?

issues.description: The current design still looks bulky and unfinished.
investigation_questions: What CSS changes are needed to reduce the card's empty space?
What template structure can create a cleaner brand/header/form/footer hierarchy?
What responsive rules are needed for mobile without overlap or horizontal scroll?

decision.reason: PM rejects the visual result. Developer must perform read-only investigation and propose a stronger revised UI plan before changing code again.
